title: Project forward while clearing an obstacle and owning an elevated landing.
brief: The seated box jump is the priority: coordinate a forward/up impulse from support and place both feet fully on a higher receiving surface. A unilateral-to-box task, one hurdle clearance, short linked hurdle contacts and rope singles address different placement/clearance demands; a seated chest pass isolates rapid forward arm force.

explosive.name: Seated Box Jump
explosive.job: Create forward/up projection from support into a higher receiving surface.
explosive.cue: Sit still with feet flat, swing the arms and jump forward/up onto a separate low stable box; hold 2 s, stand, then step down and reset.
explosive.regress: Lower/bring the landing box closer; stop for rocking, foot clipping or knee-tucking to reach a high box.

explosive.name: Single-leg Takeoff to Two-foot Box Landing
explosive.job: Apply one leg's propulsion while receiving with both feet on an elevated surface.
explosive.cue: From one foot near a low box, dip and drive forward/up, then land both feet fully on the box and hold 2 s.
explosive.regress: Lower/bring the box closer; stop for twisting takeoff or partial-foot landing.

explosive.name: Low Hurdle Forward Jump to Stick
explosive.job: Clear a small physical barrier without overreaching the forward landing.
explosive.cue: Start stationary on two feet, dip and jump over one low hurdle; land beyond it on two feet and hold 2 s.
explosive.regress: Lower the hurdle and shorten travel; stop for clipping or a feet-first reach that loses the torso.

explosive.name: Continuous Low Hurdle Hops
explosive.job: Organize successive forward contacts against an external clearance rhythm.
explosive.cue: Use two low hurdles, make two linked two-foot hops with no intentional pause, then hold the final landing 2 s.
explosive.regress: Lower/narrow the hurdle arrangement while retaining two distinct clearances; stop if rushing contact causes clipping or collapse.
explosive.note: Each rep is one hurdle clearance/landing: four total landings, not four two-hop sequences.

explosive.name: Seated Medicine Ball Chest Pass
explosive.job: Supply rapid forward arm force while keeping the leg impact dose unchanged.
explosive.cue: Sit upright on a stable bench, feet flat; release a light ball forward from chest height with a quick two-hand push, no torso heave.
explosive.regress: Use a lighter ball; stop for back arching or unsafe containment.
explosive.intent: Fast release with a light ball; retain the prescribed grounded support

explosive.name: Jump Rope Power Singles
explosive.job: Practice active foot clearance and an organized ankle return under a predictable rope passage.
explosive.cue: Use one rope turn per modest two-foot jump, six controlled contacts in place; clear the rope without tucking the knees high.
explosive.regress: Lower jump height and slow the rope to retain one turn per jump; stop after catches or disrupted landings.
explosive.intent: Crisp modest jumps; no speed/endurance target

control.name: Soleus Isometric Hold — Bent Knee
control.job: Lightly control plantarflexion with flexed knees for the box/hurdle receiving position.
control.cue: With stable hand support, bend both knees slightly and lift heels a small amount; hold knee angle and quiet forefoot contact.
control.regress: Reduce heel height/effort; stop for ankle rolling or shaking.
control.intent: Bodyweight/light resistance, easy control; at least 5 clean reps in reserve or comparable ease

control.name: Seated Band Ankle Eversion
control.job: Control the outer foot border when setting the whole foot on a receiving surface.
control.cue: Seated with heel supported, hold a light band to pull the forefoot inward; move the forefoot gently outward against it while keeping the lower leg still, then return.
control.regress: Use less tension/range; stop if the knee rotates instead of the ankle.
control.intent: Bodyweight/light resistance, easy control; at least 5 clean reps in reserve or comparable ease

strength.name: Hip Thrust — pelvic dumbbell, upper back on bench
Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated, dumbbells on thighs

decision: The elevated landing is a different support task, not evidence of a longer jump. Seated versus countermovement box takeoff changes the force-generation start; single-leg-to-box changes propulsion laterality. Hurdles impose an actual clearance constraint rather than renamed distance targets. Linked hurdle work is only four contacts; rope singles only six. Bilateral squat remains at two sets after Class 5 and other strength loads are held, preserving capacity without assuming accumulated tolerance.
next_job: Class 7 will emphasize alternating forward contacts and a controlled final stop; review actual clearance rhythm and receiving control before proceeding.
